questions.q: What does fine-tuning actually change about a model?
options: The model's weights, by continuing training on your own examples
Nothing — it only changes what's in the prompt
The vector database the model queries
The model's maximum context window size
questions.explain: Fine-tuning continues the training process on new examples, which adjusts the model's internal weights directly.

questions.q: What is fine-tuning genuinely good at?
options: Keeping facts current without ever retraining
Making citations to exact source documents
Eliminating the need for any prompt at all
Changing behavior — a consistent output format, tone, or a narrow classification skill — rather than keeping facts current
questions.explain: Fine-tuning reliably bakes in behavioral patterns like format and tone, but is a poor fit for facts that change, since every change requires retraining.

questions.q: Why is RAG better suited than fine-tuning for knowledge that changes frequently?
options: RAG lets you update an external store and have it searchable in minutes, with no retraining required
Fine-tuning is always cheaper than updating a database
RAG does not require an embedding model
RAG eliminates the need for any retrieval step
questions.explain: Because RAG keeps knowledge external in a searchable store, updating a single document takes effect immediately, unlike fine-tuning which requires retraining to reflect the same change.

questions.q: Why can RAG answers be traced to a source document, while fine-tuned knowledge generally cannot?
options: Fine-tuned models are not allowed to generate text
RAG hands the model the actual retrieved passage in the prompt, so the system can show which document it came from; fine-tuning bakes knowledge into opaque weights
RAG always includes a hyperlink automatically
Fine-tuning deletes the original training data after use
questions.explain: Because the retrieved text is explicitly part of the prompt in RAG, the system can record and display exactly which passage supported the answer — something not possible with knowledge encoded in model weights.

questions.q: According to this lesson's decision rule, when do production systems often use both RAG and fine-tuning together?
options: Never — the two approaches are mutually exclusive
Only when regulatory compliance explicitly forbids one of them
Fine-tuning the model to behave and follow instructions well, while RAG supplies current, citable facts
Only for very small models with limited context windows
questions.explain: A common pattern is fine-tuning a model to reliably follow instructions (like 'answer only from the provided context') while RAG keeps the actual factual content current and traceable.
